Located at the end of the arcade streets leading off Kokusai Street, this market is lined with Okinawan ingredients such as colorful fish, pork and island vegetables, and is called the Kitchen of Naha. Its signature is mochiage, where seafood bought on the first floor is cooked for you at the restaurants on the second floor. Experience Okinawan food culture in this lively market.
quiz_en: At Makishi Public Market, what is the system called where fish bought on the first floor is cooked for you upstairs?

desc_en: Welcome to Okinawan Eisa. This traditional performing art is danced by youth groups and others in each area during the old-calendar Obon season to welcome and send off the spirits of ancestors. Dancers parade in formation while beating large and small drums to the sanshin (three-stringed lute) and song, a truly stirring sight. The sound of drums and finger whistles echoing on summer nights is a scene that symbolizes summer in Okinawa.
quiz_en: In Eisa, what instruments do the dancers beat, and what stringed instrument is played as the accompaniment?

desc_en: Welcome to the Naha Great Tug-of-War Festival in Naha City. Held on National Route 58, this festival sees huge crowds split into east and west teams pulling a giant straw rope, and the rope is certified by Guinness World Records as the world's largest straw rope. Before the contest, hatagashira banner poles and performances in warrior costume take place, and anyone can join the tug-of-war. Experience autumn in Naha wrapped in fiery excitement.
quiz_en: The great rope used in the Naha Great Tug-of-War is certified as the world's largest rope made of what material?

desc_en: Welcome to Okinawa soba, a local dish of Okinawa. Thick noodles made from wheat flour are served in a light broth made from pork bones and bonito flakes, topped with pork belly, fish cake, pickled red ginger and more. Soki soba, topped with bone-in pork ribs, is also popular. If you like, add a seasoning of island chili peppers steeped in awamori (Okinawan distilled liquor) to enjoy a different flavor.
quiz_en: What is the seasoning called that is poured over Okinawa soba, made of island chili peppers steeped in awamori?

desc_en: Welcome to Kabira Bay in Ishigaki City. This bay in the northwest of Ishigaki Island offers scenery of emerald-green water that changes color with the time and light, white sand beaches and small green islets, one of the finest views representing Ishigaki. Black pearls are cultivated in the bay, and on a glass-bottom boat you can observe coral reefs and tropical fish. Swimming is not allowed, so enjoy the view and the scenery from the boat.
quiz_en: What shiny black gem is Kabira Bay well known for cultivating in its calm waters?

desc_en: Welcome to Ryukyu Kaiensai in Ginowan City. This fireworks festival is held at Ginowan Seaside Park, and because it takes place every spring, it is known as Japan's earliest summer fireworks. Fireworks launched one after another in time with music dye the night sea and sky in brilliant colors. Feel the warm tropical night breeze as you enjoy this dazzling light show.
quiz_en: Because of how early in the year it is held, what is the Ryukyu Kaiensai fireworks festival known as?

desc_en: Welcome to the Harvest Festival of the Yaeyama Islands. Held in summer, around the sixth month of the lunar calendar, in the villages of the islands, this festival gives thanks for the year's harvest and prays for next year's crops. Beginning with prayers at the utaki, events handed down in each village unfold, such as hatagashira banners, lion dances and a powerful tug-of-war. Feel the depth of Yaeyama culture in the fervor of a festival that unites the islanders.
quiz_en: At the Yaeyama Harvest Festival, what is the type of sacred site unique to Okinawa, used as a place of prayer, called?

desc_en: Welcome to Ishigaki Island. It is the central island of the Yaeyama Islands and the gateway to nearby islands such as Taketomi and Iriomote. Mount Omoto, the highest peak in Okinawa Prefecture, rises on the island, and diverse nature spreads out, including coral reef seas, Kabira Bay and mangroves. It is an island full of charm where you can enjoy food such as Ishigaki beef and Yaeyama soba, and a sky full of stars at night.
quiz_en: What is the name of the mountain rising in central Ishigaki Island, the highest in all of Okinawa Prefecture?

name_en: West Coast Beaches of Central and Northern Okinawa
desc_en: Welcome to the string of beaches along the west coast from central to northern Okinawa Island. Facing the East China Sea, this coastline is lined with white sandy beaches and clear water, dotted with resort hotels and beaches. The shallow sea surrounded by coral reefs is perfect for snorkeling, and in the evening the sun sinking below the horizon turns the sea gold.
quiz_en: If you were to watch the sunset from a beach on the west coast of Okinawa Island, which beach would you recommend?

desc_en: Welcome to Busena Marine Park in Kise, Nago City. This park is at the tip of Cape Busena, and from the underwater observatory reached by a bridge stretching out to sea, you can look through windows into the sea several meters deep. Its charm is observing colorful tropical fish and coral without getting wet. Head offshore on a glass-bottom boat to enjoy another side of the sea.
quiz_en: Through the windows of the underwater observatory at Busena Marine Park, what sea creature would you like to spot?

desc_en: Welcome to Nago Central Park in Nago, Nago City. This hilly park includes the Nago Castle ruins and is known as a famous spot for kanhizakura cherry blossoms that bloom in winter. Every year from January to February, it hosts one of the earliest cherry blossom festivals in Japan, with deep pink flowers coloring the hill. From the heights you can look out over the streets of Nago and Nago Bay, enjoying the view along with the blossoms.
quiz_en: What variety of cherry tree blooms in winter at Nago Central Park, with deep pink flowers that hang facing downward?

desc_en: Welcome to Okinawa Peace Memorial Park in Mabuni, Itoman City. Laid out on Mabuni Hill, regarded as the place where the Battle of Okinawa ended, the park holds the Cornerstone of Peace, engraved with the names of the war dead regardless of nationality or whether military or civilian, as well as the Peace Memorial Museum. A memorial ceremony is held on June 23, Okinawa Memorial Day. On this hill overlooking the blue sea, reflect on the preciousness of peace.
quiz_en: What is the monument in the Peace Memorial Park, engraved with the names of those who died in the Battle of Okinawa, called?

desc_en: Welcome to the Katsuren Castle ruins in Katsuren, Uruma City. This gusuku (Okinawan castle) was built on a hill on the Katsuren Peninsula and is known as the residence of the local lord Amawari; it is also a component of a World Heritage site. Curving stone walls rise in tiers, and from the top you can see Nakagusuku Bay and the islands of the Pacific. Climb the stone steps in the sea breeze and imagine its past prosperity.
quiz_en: What is the name of the lord known as master of Katsuren Castle, whose story is passed down in kumiodori dance dramas?

desc_en: Welcome to Yonaha Maehama in Miyakojima City. This white sandy beach stretches about 7 km along the southwest of Miyako Island and is sometimes praised as the most beautiful in the Orient. The contrast between the fine sand and the clear sea known as Miyako Blue is stunning. Offshore stretches the Kurima Bridge to Kurima Island, and you can also enjoy marine sports and sunset views.
quiz_en: The bridge that stretches offshore from Yonaha Maehama connects Miyako Island with which other island?

desc_en: Welcome to Cape Higashi-Hennazaki in Miyakojima City. This long, narrow cape juts from the eastern tip of Miyako Island into the Pacific, and its charm is the grand view of deep blue sea spreading on both sides. A white lighthouse stands at the tip, and if you climb it you can see the whole cape and the sea. In spring, Easter lilies bloom all over the cape, and the combination of white flowers and blue sea is magnificent.
quiz_en: What is the name of the lily that blooms in spring at Cape Higashi-Hennazaki, covering the whole cape in white?

desc_en: Welcome to Yabiji in Miyakojima City. Spreading north of Ikema Island, it is one of the largest coral reef groups in Japan, with many reefs gathered to form a vast underwater landscape. At low tide during the spring tides, the reefs emerge above the sea surface, and it is also called the Phantom Continent. Snorkeling and diving let you enjoy a world of colorful coral and tropical fish.
quiz_en: Around which day of which month in the old lunar calendar does the spring tide reveal most of Yabiji above the sea?

desc_en: Welcome to Miyako Island. Because this flat island has no large rivers or mountains, little soil flows into the sea, and highly transparent water called Miyako Blue spreads around it. The Irabu Bridge to Irabu Island is among the longest toll-free bridges in Japan, and driving over the sea is exhilarating. Tour the peaceful landscapes of sugarcane fields and the beautiful beaches.
quiz_en: What is the name of the long bridge that runs over the sea and connects Miyako Island with Irabu Island?

desc_en: Welcome to Gyokusendo in Tamagusuku, Nanjo City. This limestone cave lies within the theme park Okinawa World, where countless stalactites and stalagmites formed over long ages emerge magically under the lighting. The cave is one of the largest in Japan, and highlights appear one after another, such as pools fed by underground water and clusters of icicle-like stalactites.
quiz_en: What is the name of the theme park, where you can also enjoy Okinawan culture, that contains the Gyokusendo cave in Nanjo City?

desc_en: Welcome to Kudaka Island in Nanjo City. This small island floats in the sea east of southern Okinawa Island and has long been revered as the Island of the Gods, which appears in the Ryukyu creation myth. The island has many places regarded as sacred, which are still carefully protected. As you tour the island by bicycle, follow the rules and feel its white beaches, quiet village and the prayerful air that flows through it.
quiz_en: Which World Heritage sacred site in Nanjo City is also known as a place for worshipping Kudaka Island from afar?

desc_en: Welcome to the plant communities of Yanbaru in Kunigami Village. In Yanbaru, the northern part of Okinawa Island, a subtropical forest thick with evergreen broadleaf trees such as itajii spreads out, and it is registered as a World Natural Heritage site. The forest is home to creatures found nowhere else, such as the flightless Okinawa rail. Feel the breath of life in this rich forest.
quiz_en: What is the name of the bird living in the Yanbaru forest that can hardly fly at all?

desc_en: Welcome to Hiji Falls in Hiji, Kunigami Village. This waterfall lies deep in the Yanbaru forest and has one of the greatest drops on Okinawa Island. The trail from the entrance through the subtropical forest is a trekking course that crosses a suspension bridge and follows a clear stream. The sight of the falls cascading down the rock face at the end is moving, and you can bask in plenty of fresh, negative-ion-rich air.
quiz_en: When you walked the Yanbaru forest trail to Hiji Falls, what kinds of creatures did you come across?

desc_en: Welcome to Daisekirinzan in Hedo, Kunigami Village. Near Cape Hedo at the northern tip of Okinawa Island, this mountain of strange rocks was formed as limestone eroded over long ages, displaying a tropical karst landscape. Walking the trails where sharp rocks stand like a forest, you will encounter oddly shaped rocks one after another. From the observation deck you can look out over the East China Sea and the Pacific Ocean.
quiz_en: What do you call landforms like those of Daisekirinzan, created when limestone is dissolved by rainwater?

desc_en: Welcome to the Nakijin Castle ruins in Nakijin Village. During the Three Kingdoms period, when Ryukyu was divided into three powers, this gusuku was the residence of the King of Hokuzan, and it is a component of a World Heritage site. The long stone walls stretching in waves are truly impressive, and from the ruins you can look out over the East China Sea. From January to February, kanhizakura cherries bloom, a season when the stone walls and blossoms make a beautiful pair.
quiz_en: During the Three Kingdoms period of Ryukyu, what was the power that ruled northern Okinawa Island from Nakijin Castle called?

desc_en: Welcome to Ocean Expo Park in Motobu Town. This vast park was developed on the former site of the Okinawa International Ocean Exposition, and its centerpiece is the Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium. In the huge tank recreating the Kuroshio Current, you can watch whale sharks and manta rays swimming leisurely. With dolphin shows, tropical plant displays, Emerald Beach and more, it has attractions to enjoy all day long.
quiz_en: What is the name of the world's largest fish, which swims in the giant tank of the Churaumi Aquarium?

desc_en: Welcome to the Motobu Yaedake Cherry Blossom Festival in Motobu Town. Numerous kanhizakura cherry trees are planted along the mountain road of Mount Yaedake, and from late January to February their deep pink flowers bloom together. It is one of the earliest cherry blossom festivals in Japan, and the avenue of cherry trees leading up the mountain is a true tunnel of blossoms. Feel an early spring in Okinawa, warm even in winter.
quiz_en: What variety of cherry tree, which blooms in winter in Okinawa, decorates the cherry-lined road of Motobu Yaedake?

desc_en: Welcome to Cape Maeda in Maeda, Onna Village. This cliffside cape faces the East China Sea, and the sea cave beneath it, the Blue Cave, is a mysterious place where light streaming in makes the water glow blue. It is a popular snorkeling and diving spot, with many tropical fish swimming in the clear sea. From the observation deck atop the cape, you can look out over the emerald sea.
quiz_en: What is the cave beneath Cape Maeda called, where light streams in and makes the sea surface glow blue?

desc_en: Welcome to Ie Island. This flat island lies off the Motobu Peninsula, and in its center Gusuku Yama, called Tacchu, rises strikingly high. From the summit you can see the whole island and the surrounding sea, and on clear days even the mountains of the main island. In spring, Easter lilies bloom across a park on the island, and a carpet of white flowers welcomes visitors.
quiz_en: By what affectionate nickname is Gusuku Yama, the peak rising in the center of Ie Island, known locally?

desc_en: Welcome to Cape Zanpa in Yomitan Village. Cliffs around 30 meters high continue for about 2 km along this cape, where rough waves crash in a powerful landscape. The white Cape Zanpa Lighthouse stands at the tip, and if you climb it you can see across the East China Sea. The cape park also has a large shisa statue, and at dusk the sunset sinking into the sea is spectacular.
quiz_en: The large statue in the Cape Zanpa park depicts what kind of animal, regarded in Okinawa as a guardian against evil?

desc_en: Welcome to the Zakimi Castle ruins in Zakimi, Yomitan Village. This gusuku is said to have been built in the early 15th century by Gosamaru, a master castle builder, and is a component of a World Heritage site. Its elegant curving walls and arched gate fitted with a keystone are praised as among the most beautiful of the gusuku remaining in Okinawa. From the ruins on the heights, you can look out over the village of Yomitan and the sea.
quiz_en: Who is the lord, known as a master castle builder, who is said to have built Zakimi Castle?

desc_en: Welcome to Himawari in Kitanakagusuku in Kisaba, Kitanakagusuku Village. This sunflower field event blooms in winter, letting you enjoy a scene unique to warm Okinawa, with yellow flowers spreading across the fields in midwinter. Walking among sunflowers turned toward the sun under a blue sky will put you in such a bright mood that you forget the season. It is a flower field perfect for taking photos.
quiz_en: At Himawari in Kitanakagusuku, in which surprising season of the year are the sunflowers in bloom?

desc_en: Welcome to the Nakagusuku Castle ruins in Ogusuku, Kitanakagusuku Village. This gusuku is known for having Gosamaru as its lord and is a component of a World Heritage site. Stone walls skillfully built of cut stones form six enclosures, and their high level of craftsmanship is said to have been praised by Perry's party, who visited at the end of the Edo period. From the heights, a view spreads over both Nakagusuku Bay and the East China Sea.
quiz_en: Which American commodore visited the Nakagusuku Castle ruins at the end of the Edo period and praised its stonework?

desc_en: Welcome to Tokashiki Island. Reached by boat from Tomari Port in Naha, this island of the Kerama Islands is surrounded by crystal-clear water called Kerama Blue. At Aharen Beach and Tokashiku Beach, you can meet colorful fish and coral while snorkeling. From winter to spring, you can also enjoy whale watching, as humpback whales visit the nearby waters.
quiz_en: What is the name given to the highly transparent sea color of the Kerama Islands, including Tokashiki Island?

desc_en: Welcome to the coasts of the Kerama Islands, spanning Tokashiki and Zamami Villages. These waters, dotted with islands large and small, are known for their astonishingly clear Kerama Blue sea and are designated a national park. White sandy beaches and coral reefs continue one after another, and the area is famous as a dream destination for divers. In winter, humpback whales come here to raise their young.
quiz_en: What species of large whale comes to the sea around the Kerama Islands in winter to raise its young?

desc_en: Welcome to Zamami Island. One of the Kerama Islands, it is dotted with beautiful beaches of clear water, such as Furuzamami Beach. From winter to spring, humpback whales appear in the nearby waters, making it popular as a base for whale watching. From the island's observation decks, superb views of the surrounding islands and sea spread out, and you can spend relaxed island time.
quiz_en: What are the tours called that let you observe whales around Zamami Island from winter through spring?

desc_en: Welcome to Minamidaito Island. This island lies in the Pacific far east of Okinawa Island, and its settlement began in the Meiji era with people from Hachijojima. Because it is surrounded by cliffs, people are sometimes lifted on and off ships by crane at the port. Sugarcane fields spread across this island with a unique culture, where you can also taste its specialty, Daito sushi.
quiz_en: From which island did the people who began settling Minamidaito Island in the Meiji era originally come?

desc_en: Welcome to Iheya Island. The northernmost inhabited island in Okinawa Prefecture, it offers green mountains, beautiful sandy beaches and peaceful farmland. Rice has been grown here since long ago, and a calm island way of life still lives on. There are many sights, such as a cave linked to the Amano-Iwato legend and a famous pine tree with widely spreading branches, so you can leisurely enjoy the nature of sea and mountains.
quiz_en: Among the inhabited islands of Okinawa Prefecture, Iheya Island lies at the far end in which direction?

name_en: Coasts of Iheya and Izena (Nohokome Cape, Futamigaura)
desc_en: Welcome to the coasts of Iheya and Izena Islands. These two islands north of Okinawa Island are dotted with beautiful shores where white sand, rocks and clear water come together, such as Kome Cape on Noho Island and Futamigaura on Izena Island. With few visitors, their charm is spending time on a quiet beach listening only to the sound of the waves.
quiz_en: On a quiet, uncrowded beach on a remote island, what is the one thing you would most like to do?

desc_en: Welcome to Izena Island. This island north of Okinawa Island is known as the birthplace of King Sho En, who founded the Second Sho Dynasty of the Ryukyu Kingdom. Historic sites linked to King Sho En remain, and traditional village scenery, with red-tiled houses, stone walls and windbreaks of fukugi trees, is carefully preserved. It is an island where you can experience both beautiful seas and history.
quiz_en: Who was the king, born on Izena Island, who founded the Second Sho Dynasty of the Ryukyu Kingdom?

desc_en: Welcome to Hatenohama in Kumejima Town. Off the east coast of Kume Island, this sandbar made only of white sand stretches for several kilometers. Surrounded by emerald-green sea, the sight of a pure white beach with no buildings or trees looks like another world. You can cross on a tour boat and enjoy snorkeling and beach walks. Don't forget to protect yourself from the strong sun.
quiz_en: What do you call a landform like Hatenohama, a long, narrow beach made only of sand that extends into the sea?

desc_en: Welcome to Kume Island. This lush island west of Okinawa Island is blessed with spring water and has long been called the Island of Kumi (beauty). Kumejima tsumugi, handed down on the island, is a traditional textile known for its subdued colors dyed with plant dyes. The island is full of sights, such as Tatami-ishi, where rocks resembling turtle shells line up, and Hatenohama offshore.
quiz_en: What is the traditional textile of Kume Island, woven from threads dyed with plants, called?

desc_en: Welcome to the Yaese Cherry Blossom Festival in Tomori, Yaese Town. Held at Yaese Park, this festival sees winter-blooming kanhizakura cherries dye the park deep pink. During the festival, lights are lit for enjoying the blossoms at night, and the park bustles with local performing arts and food stalls. The view from the park on the heights is also good, making it a flower festival of southern Okinawa where you can feel the early arrival of spring.
quiz_en: If you were viewing the cherry blossoms at night at the Yaese Cherry Blossom Festival, what Okinawan food would you like to eat?

desc_en: Welcome to Minna Island in Motobu Town. This small, flat island off the Motobu Peninsula is also called Croissant Island because of its shape seen from the air. You can reach it in a short time by high-speed boat and enjoy snorkeling and swimming on its white sandy beaches and clear sea. In the relaxed island atmosphere, enjoy the tropical sea to the fullest.
quiz_en: Because of its shape when seen from the air, Minna Island is compared to what kind of bread?

desc_en: Welcome to the Urauchi River on Iriomote Island. It is the longest river in Okinawa Prefecture, with mangrove forests spreading near its mouth. As you travel upriver on a sightseeing boat, subtropical jungle scenery continues, and upstream you can trek to Mariyudu Falls and Kanpire Falls. Paddling along the river by canoe lets you feel the rich nature of Iriomote up close.
quiz_en: What is the forest called that grows near the mouth of the Urauchi River, where seawater and fresh water mix?

desc_en: Welcome to the coasts of Hateruma Island. Known as Japan's southernmost inhabited island, Hateruma is surrounded by a vivid sea praised as Hateruma Blue. The gradation of the sea seen from the white sands of Nishihama Beach is breathtakingly beautiful. At the southern tip of the island stands the monument marking Japan's southernmost point, and when conditions are right you can see the Southern Cross in the night sky.
quiz_en: What constellation, representative of the Southern Hemisphere, can be seen from Hateruma Island when conditions are good?

desc_en: Welcome to the coasts of Aragusuku Island in Taketomi Town. Aragusuku consists of two islands, Kamiji and Shimoji, and is also called Panari. It is surrounded by highly transparent water ringed by coral reefs, and untouched nature remains with pure white beaches. The islands have many carefully protected sacred sites, so when visiting, follow the island rules and quietly savor the beauty of the sea.
quiz_en: Aragusuku Island consists of Kamiji and Shimoji Islands. By what nickname is it known among locals?

desc_en: Welcome to the plant communities along the Nakama River on Iriomote Island. One of the largest mangrove forests in Japan spreads along the lower Nakama River and is designated a National Natural Monument. Traveling upstream by sightseeing boat, you will see forests of mangrove trees covering both banks, and upstream stands a large Sakishima suou tree with plank-like roots. Encounter the curious forms of the subtropical forest.
quiz_en: What is the name of the large tree standing on the upper Nakama River, known for its distinctive plank-like roots?

desc_en: Welcome to the red-tiled houses of Taketomi Island. In this village, houses with red-tiled roofs surrounded by coral stone walls line white sand roads, and it has been selected as an Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings. Shisa guardian figures sit on the roofs, and flowers such as bougainvillea add color. Ride a slow-moving water buffalo cart and enjoy the traditional island scenery.
quiz_en: In the village of Taketomi Island, what is the cart called that is pulled by a slow-walking animal carrying tourists?

desc_en: Welcome to Taketomi Island. A short boat ride from Ishigaki Island, this small island has a village of red-tiled houses and white sand roads that is said to be the original landscape of Okinawa. Kaiji Beach is known for star-shaped sand, and the shallow waters of Kondoi Beach are beautiful too. Tour the island at leisure by bicycle or water buffalo cart, and watch the sunset from Nishi Pier in the evening.
quiz_en: What is the star-shaped sand called that you can search for on Kaiji Beach on Taketomi Island?

desc_en: Welcome to Iriomote Island. Most of this island, the second largest in Okinawa Prefecture, is covered in subtropical primeval forest, and it is registered as a World Natural Heritage site. Rare creatures live here, including the Iriomote cat found only on this island. Paddling a canoe up mangrove rivers or heading for waterfalls deep in the jungle, it is an island that stirs your spirit of adventure.
quiz_en: What is the wild cat found only on Iriomote Island, designated a Special Natural Monument of Japan?

desc_en: Welcome to Kohama Island. Located almost in the center of the Yaeyama Islands, the island's central peak, Mount Ufudaki, offers a panoramic view of the surrounding islands and coral reef seas. The Sugar Road, running straight between sugarcane fields, is a popular road that also served as a setting for an NHK morning drama series. Feel the peaceful island time as you tour the island at a relaxed pace.
quiz_en: What is the title of the NHK morning drama series that was set on Kohama Island?

desc_en: Welcome to Kuroshima in Taketomi Town. This flat island is known for its shape, which looks like a heart, and with its spreading ranches it is an island of cattle, said to have more cows than residents. The landscape of cattle grazing leisurely, endless pastures and the coral reef sea is peace itself. In summer, it is also known as a nesting site for sea turtles.
quiz_en: Kuroshima is known for having more of something than it has residents. What is there more of?

desc_en: Welcome to Yonaguni Island. Located at the westernmost point of Japan, this border island sometimes offers a view of Taiwan across the sea from Cape Irizaki on clear days. Native Yonaguni horses live leisurely on the island, and its charm is grand scenery of cliffs and grasslands. Under the sea lie huge rock formations, popular as a diving spot.
quiz_en: From the cape at the westernmost tip of Yonaguni Island, what place can sometimes be seen on clear days?
